_comment_fallback: html and pdf must be excluded, and /handbook/* with them. An iframe load is a navigation request, so without this the browser asking for /handbook/book.html was rewritten to the SPA shell — while curl, which sends no navigate mode, got the real file and made it look fine.
_comment_frame: SAMEORIGIN, not DENY: DENY blocks framing by anyone including this origin, which broke the handbook page embedding its own /handbook/index.html. SAMEORIGIN still refuses every other site, which is the clickjacking threat.

globalHeaders.Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'sha256-PZveF1zDrsWvdm4u7R25zgs/J4/wvtljs+BZfPKCYbg='; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: blob: https://API_ORIGIN_PLACEHOLDER; font-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self' https://API_ORIGIN_PLACEHOLDER; worker-src 'self' blob:; frame-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'self'

_comment_csp: The app loads nothing from anywhere but itself and the API. script-src carries the sha256 of the one inline script in index.html — the theme check that sets data-theme before first paint, so dark mode does not flash white. EDITING THAT SCRIPT CHANGES ITS HASH: recompute it or the browser will refuse to run it and dark mode will flash on every load. style-src allows inline because React writes style attributes. img-src and connect-src name the API because avatars and every request go there; blob: and data: are for the PDF export (jspdf/html2canvas). frame-src self is the handbook, which embeds its own page.
